experiment: E10: UML3 IDL v1 parser against 701 third-party IDL files (external/idl submodules)
outcomes: ACCEPT (parsed, SysML emitted), UNSUPPORTED (IdlException naming an out-of-scope construct), REJECT (other IdlException), CRASH (any non-IdlException Throwable), TIMEOUT (>10 s)

predictions.claim: Fewer than 40% of the files not known to be invalid are ACCEPTed (CORBA valuetypes, #include-dependent files, #define macros, bitsets/maps are common)
At least 1 file CRASHes (non-IdlException, e.g. index or cast errors on unexpected syntax): the parser was only exercised on its own fixtures
0 TIMEOUTs: every parser loop consumes a token or throws
At least 30% of the known-invalid files (JacORB compiler/fail, ic-hir tests/fail) are wrongly ACCEPTed, because v1 does no semantic checks (name resolution, duplicates, type compatibility)
Every ACCEPTed file has a stable canonical round trip (write -> parse -> write identical)
